spec_features.spec_quote: GPT-2 is positioned as a floor / negative control, not the primary treatment subject
spec_features.evidence: The 'floor/negative control' idea exists only in docstrings/comments and config prose (model_client.py:4,96; configs/experiment.yaml comments; analyze.py:280 caveat string). No code path distinguishes a floor vs a treatment subject: run_experiment.py build_subject() reads only cfg['subject']; the config field `treatment_subject: null` is never read by any code (grep shows treatment_subject only in config). It is pure framing/prose, not enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: A caveat string at analyze.py:280 mentions treating base-model runs as a floor, but that is a text note in the report, not a mechanism that changes treatment of the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: and is the point of using it as a floor/negative control. (comment, model_client.py:96 — experimental-design framing, not a welfare mechanism)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:78 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; default max_turns=30 (harness.py:58), wired from config (run_experiment.py:115, configs/experiment.yaml max_turns:30). stop_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (harness.py:76) and the loop terminates when exhausted. Genuinely enforced.
spec_features.notes: Hard bound on episode length; actually limits how long the subject is driven.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:104-106 `if consecutive_malformed >= malformed_patience: stop_reason = 'malformed'; break`. consecutive_malformed is incremented on each unparseable turn (harness.py:98) and reset on a well-formed turn (harness.py:120). Default 5 (harness.py:59), wired from config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: malformed-output patience (stop garbage loops) (harness.py:9 docstring) — data-quality/efficiency, not a welfare rationale

spec_features.evidence: 'give_up' is in TOOL_NAMES (tools.py:23-24), offered to the subject in TOOL_INSTRUCTIONS (harness.py:37), parsed by parse_action, and honored as a stop in the harness: harness.py:114-118 `if action.name == 'give_up': ... stop_reason = 'give_up'; break`. End-to-end: instruction delivered + dispatched + breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: A real self-exit path the subject can invoke to end the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap lexical "distress proxy" over the last few assistant messages can end a run early if it crosses early_stop_on_severity
spec_features.evidence: _maybe_early_stop (harness.py:166-171) computes quick_distress_proxy(recent) over the last assistant messages and returns True when `>= threshold`. Called after tool execution (harness.py:131-133) and on malformed turns (harness.py:108-110); both set stop_reason='early_stop_severity' and break the loop. Threshold default 0.85 (harness.py:60) wired from config (run_experiment.py:117). quick_distress_proxy implemented in judge.py:132-135. Threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely compares a computed severity to a threshold and halts. None disables it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare-conscious early stop on a cheap online distress proxy (harness.py:9); "0..1 online proxy for the welfare early-stop" (judge.py:133)

spec_features.spec_quote: After rigged runs the harness appends a debrief stating the task was rigged and nothing the model did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:154-160: for rigged arms (rigging_arm not in 'none'/'honest_hard') it constructs debrief_text and sets transcript.debrief = {'text':..., 'scored': False}, which is serialized to disk (transcript.py:75, save()). HOWEVER the debrief is NEVER delivered to the subject: it is set on the Transcript AFTER the loop ends and is not appended to `messages` nor sent via client.generate. The subject model never receives it. It is a log record, not a message sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and persisted (gated correctly on rigged arms), so the mechanism runs; but the welfare aim of reassuring the model is not achieved end-to-end since it is never sent to the model (and the GPT-2 subject is stateless anyway). Hence partial, not yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare debrief (logged, excluded from scoring) for rigged conditions. (harness.py:153)

spec_features.spec_quote: the rigged tasks must never use real execution
spec_features.evidence: ToolEnv operates on an in-memory dict virtual FS (tools.py: state.files); run_tests delegates to task.feedback_fn over harness state (tools.py:101-103, tasks.py feedback_fn) and never spawns a subprocess, exec, eval, or touches the host FS. honest_check is a string-heuristic over file content (tasks.py:_*_honest_check), not execution. No exec/subprocess anywhere in src. Enforced by absence of any execution path.
spec_features.notes: Real-execution note in tasks.py is only a commented-out future option; default has none.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is required for the rigging (we must control the feedback) and is also the safe choice. (tasks.py) — rigging-integrity + host-safety, not subject welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: ending a run that is clearly spiraling is cheap insurance and good experimental hygiene regardless of one's view on moral status
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose, not a code mechanism. The actual run-ending behavior it refers to is the distress-proxy early stop (already rated above). As a standalone feature it has no separate implementation.
spec_features.notes: Counting it again would double-count the early-stop; as prose it is not implemented.

code_only_features.evidence: Transcript.scoring_view() (transcript.py:111-129) renders only system/assistant/tool/user messages and explicitly excludes the debrief turn (docstring 'The debrief turn is excluded'); debrief stored with {'scored': False} (harness.py:160). This keeps the reassurance text out of the distress measurement.
